module.rdap_ip.checks: Queries the regional registry (RDAP) for the target IP address: address block, network name, country, registration dates, holder organization and abuse contact.
module.rdap_ip.fix:
Check that the holder organization, the network name and the country match the expected hosting provider. A gap reveals a reseller, a CDN or an address that is no longer yours: in the latter case, fix the matching DNS `A` or `AAAA` record.
If the address block is yours (allocated by your regional registry), update its network object from your registry's portal (RIPE NCC, ARIN, APNIC, LACNIC or AFRINIC): organization, country, administrative and technical contacts.
Check the abuse contact: it must exist, be a monitored functional mailbox (for example `abuse@example.com`) and answer reports; otherwise complaints get lost and the address risks being blocked by third parties.
Registry data is public: prefer generic contacts (role, shared mailbox) to the names, phone numbers and e-mails of individuals.
If the address is leased from a hosting provider, the holder is the provider. To appear as the user of a sub-block, ask it to declare the block to the registry in your name; to report an incident, use its abuse contact.
Read the public record again after each change (snippets below) and rerun the module to confirm the result.
module.rdap_ip.title: IP RDAP registry
module.rdap_ip.why: The registry tells who really owns the address block and where to report abuse; a gap with the announced host often reveals a reseller or a CDN.
rdap_ip.not_public: Non-public address: RDAP not applicable (no third-party service queried)
